The fed funds rate is about 1.42%, the 10-year yield is 2.90%, unemployment is 4.1%, and the VIX is 18.59 after a 1-month equity drop of 4.6% (the early-February 2018 selloff). The dollar is down 7% year over year, which also fits early 2018. Equities fell 4.6% in the month and the VIX rose 7.3 points over three months. February 2018 would fit better, since the S&P fell about 3.7% that month and the VIX closed near 19.8. January 2018 had equities up. A fed funds rate of 1.42% matches February 2018 (1.41%). So the month is February 2018.
